kind: mid-work adversarial review, before the PR is opened
subAgents: none. No sub-agent was spawned; the dispatch forbids it. Nothing was delegated and nothing was interrupted.

localVerification.npm test: exit 0, 74 tests, 73 pass, 1 skipped (vendor-parity arm B, which needs SC_DASHBOARDS_DIR and is set only in CI)
localVerification.npm run prove:gates: exit 0, 22 of 22 injected violations caught and named, 6 of them new
localVerification.npm run prove:fonts: exit 0, both families loaded and both measurably changed the rendering

defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.what: The font-load proof measured the wrong font and passed.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.how: The probe page set font-family in a style ATTRIBUTE. The token value contains double quotes, so the attribute terminated at the first one and both probes silently inherited the body font. Both live probes then measured 2773.2px, identically, while the check reported success.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.caught: by reconciling two numbers that should have differed and did not, per DEV_PROCESS 1.4. Nothing in the run said anything was wrong.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.fix: the probe styles moved into a generated style block; the page now reports getComputedStyle().fontFamily for every probe; a new assertion fails if the computed family does not start with the family being proven, and another fails if two token stacks measure the same width.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.afterFix: IBM Plex Mono measures 3180.00px for a 53-character string at 100px, which is 53 x 60px, the exact 0.6em advance of a real monospace face. Before the fix it measured 2773.2px, which was Inter.

defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.what: document.fonts.check() cannot fire, so it was worthless as the gating indicator.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.how: Watched: with every Inter @font-face rule removed, check('400 100px "Inter"') still returned true for all four weights. An undeclared family is treated as an available system font.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.fix: the assertion moved to the FontFaceSet itself, where an entry exists only because a rule declared it and reaches status loaded only when its file was fetched and parsed. check() is still printed, labelled a diagnostic, and asserted on nothing.
defectsFoundInMyOwnInstrument.provenAbleToFire: with Inter removed the run exits 1 naming 'Inter 400 is declared by no @font-face rule' for all four weights and 'measures identically with and without the shipped family'.

adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.question: Can the exception widen without a test failing?
adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.answer: Not by any route found. Every rule in the sheet must be an @font-face with the prelude matched exactly; content outside any rule fails; a nested at-rule fails because its outer brace cannot pair. Six injected violations are watched failing.

adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.question: Does the byte equality of kit.css still hold?
adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.answer: Yes, unchanged, and now also asserted to carry no @font-face with the reason attached, so a future hand that folds them in fails with an explanation rather than a diff.

adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.question: Is the weight set a decision this package makes?
adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.answer: No, and that is enforced. Both the fetch script and the gate parse the same font URL out of vendor/index.html through one imported parser. The gate fails in both directions: a weight the product asks for and the package lacks, and a weight the package carries that the product does not ask for.

adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.question: Could the gate pass with the fonts absent?
adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.answer: No. The inverse assertion fails against the tree as it stood before this change: a family a font token names first must have at least one face. That case is in prove:gates as 'the original defect'.

adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.question: Does the consumer actually receive the files?
adversarialReviewOfTheDeliverable.answer: Checked against the tarball, not against dist/: every url() in the PACKED fonts.css must match an entry in the tarball listing, and at least two licence texts must be inside dist/fonts/.

openRisksCarriedIntoTheClose: prove:fonts is now a CI step and has never run on Linux. If google-chrome is absent or the Linux fallback stack measures identically, CI fails and I fix it there; the step fails loudly rather than skipping.
The proof runs against dist/, not against an installed tarball. The tarball path is covered by static assertion only.
No bundler is exercised. A consumer whose bundler rewrites url() in CSS is not represented by any test here.
constraintsHonored: vendor/sc-kit.css and vendor/shell.css untouched (arm A hash check passes)
no component, class or rule that styles a component added
no LICENSE file added; the two OFL texts are the fonts' own licence
no forbidden string in any shipping file: the constraints suite passes and the seven needles were additionally run over all 43 woff2 files and both licence texts, zero hits
